chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Ḥammād narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
A man said to him, "I forget the recitation in the first rakʿah." He said, "Recite in the second."
He said, "I said: I forget in the second." He said, "Recite in the third."
He said, "I said: I forget throughout my whole prayer." So he said, "If you have preserved the rukūʿ and the sujūd, then your salat is complete."

key_terms.أَسْهُو: I forget or become inattentive during the prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتُكَ: your salat, meaning the prayer being performed

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forget the recitation in one or more rakʿahs of salat?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses forgetfulness in salat, specifically missing the recitation in successive rakʿahs. It indicates that if one forgets recitation, it may be made up in a later rakʿah, and that the salat remains complete so long as its essential acts, especially rukūʿ and sujūd, are preserved.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1004 - Hussain ibn Hammad narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that a man said to him: "I forget the recitation in the first rak'ah."

The man then said: "I forget in the second rak'ah as well."
Imam (as) said: "Recite in the third."

The man said: "I forget throughout my entire prayer."
Imam (as) said: "If you have remembered the ruku' (bowing) and Sujood (prostration), then your prayer is complete."
